'''Jerrelle Benimon''' (born August 1, 1991) is an American former professional [[basketball]] player. In college, he was the 2012–13 [[Colonial Athletic Association Men's Basketball Player of the Year|Colonial Athletic Association Player of the Year]] as a [[redshirt (sports)|redshirt]] junior after leading the [[Towson Tigers men's basketball|Towson Tigers]] to the greatest single-season turnaround in [[National Collegiate Athletic Association]] (NCAA) [[Division I (NCAA)|Division I]] history; the Tigers finished with a 1–31 record in 2011–12 before completing an 18–13 season the following year. Benimon also tied for the second-highest rebounding average (11.2) in Division I behind only [[Siena Saints men's basketball|Siena]]'s [[O. D. Anosike]]'s 11.4 per game average. Benimon repeated as the player of the year as a [[senior (education)|senior]] in 2013–14 and, coincidentally, finished second in the national rebounding average for a second consecutive season (11.2).

==High school career==
Benimon attended [[Fauquier High School]] in [[Warrenton, Virginia]].<ref name=BIO>{{cite web|title=Jerrelle Benimon biography |work=TowsonTigers.com |publisher=[[Towson University]] |date=March 25, 2013 |url=http://www.towsontigers.com/ViewArticle.dbml?DB_OEM_ID=21300&ATCLID=205177711 |access-date=March 30, 2013 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130619062626/http://www.towsontigers.com/ViewArticle.dbml?DB_OEM_ID=21300&ATCLID=205177711 |archive-date=June 19, 2013 }}</ref> In his junior season in 2007–08 he averaged 19.5 points, 12.5 rebounds, 3.4 blocks and 3.5 assists per game.<ref name=BIO/> Then, as a senior, he averaged 21 points, 17 rebounds, 7 assists and 4 blocks per game en route to his second consecutive Cedar Run District Player of the Year award.<ref name=BIO/> On February 17, 2009, Benimon recorded a [[quadruple-double]] against [[Osbourn High School]] with 13 points, 17 rebounds, 11 assists, 10 blocks.<ref name=BIO/>

==College career==
Benimon spent his first two collegiate seasons playing for the [[Georgetown Hoyas men's basketball|Hoyas]] of [[Georgetown University]].<ref name=SR>{{cite web|title=Jerrelle Benimon stats |work=sports-reference.com |publisher=Sports Reference LLC |date=March 30, 2013 |url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cbb/players/jerrelle-benimon-1.html |access-date=March 30, 2013 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130328044604/http://www.sports-reference.com/cbb/players/jerrelle-benimon-1.html |archive-date=March 28, 2013 }}</ref> He saw limited action in both seasons and scored a total of 84 points in 61 game appearances.<ref name=SR/> He decided to transfer after his sophomore year in 2010–11, one in which he only averaged 10.2 minutes per game.<ref name=SR/> Benimon said he "probably got 100 phone calls" from schools who were trying to recruit him as a transfer player, but he ultimately decided on Towson because "...the assistant that recruited me from Towson. He treated me like a big deal. He’d send me an e-mail 1,000 times a day. He’d call me all the time."<ref name=FAUQUIER>{{cite web| last =Rummel| first =Joe| title =Towson junior and Fauquier High grad Jerrelle Benimon answers all questions| publisher =Fauquier.com| date =March 6, 2013| url =http://www.fauquier.com/index.php/news/article/towson_junior_and_fauquier_high_grad_jerrelle_benimon_answers_all_questions| access-date = March 30, 2013}}</ref>

Having to sit out the 2011–12 season due to NCAA by-laws, Benimon flew under the radar heading in the [[Colonial Athletic Association]]'s 2012–13 season.<ref name=SLAM>{{cite web| last =Fischer| first =Jake| title =Unexpected Journey: How the improbable CAA Player of the Year led Towson to an improbable turnaround| work =[[SLAM Magazine]]| publisher =Source Interlink Magazines, LLC| date =March 13, 2013| url =http://www.slamonline.com/online/college-hs/college/slammadness/2013/03/jerrelle-benimon-unexpected-journey/| access-date = March 30, 2013}}</ref> He was not even selected to an All-CAA team during the conference's preseason media day.<ref name=SLAM/> Benimon burst onto the national scene during his junior year after averaging 17.1 points, 11.2 rebounds, 2.5 assists and 1.9 blocks per game.<ref name=SLAM/> He was named the CAA Player of the Week four times, its player of the year at the end of the regular season, and guided its 17.5-game turnaround from 2011–12 (the biggest turnaround in Division I history) by leading Towson in points, rebounds, assists and blocks.<ref name=BIO/><ref name=FAUQUIER/><ref name=SLAM/> In an early season loss against [[2012–13 Temple Owls men's basketball team|Temple]], Benimon scored 30 points and grabbed 18 rebounds; in an improbable road win against [[2012–13 Oregon State Beavers men's basketball team|Oregon State]], he recorded 20 points and 21 rebounds.<ref name=SLAM/> Benimon was a top 10 finalist for the [[Lou Henson Award]], given to the nation's best [[mid-major]] men's basketball player.<ref>{{cite web| last =Phelan| first =Sean| title =Towson's Own Jerrelle Benimon A Finalist For Lou Henson Award| publisher =Towson University| date =March 6, 2013| url =http://tutigerstoday.towson.edu/?p=91923| access-date = March 30, 2013}}</ref>

Benimon's senior season in 2013–14 saw him lead the Tigers to a second-place finish in the CAA behind [[2013–14 Delaware Fightin' Blue Hens men's basketball team|Delaware]], finishing the year with a 13–3 conference record (25–11 overall).<ref name=SCHED>{{cite web| title =Towson Tigers Basketball 2013–14 Schedule| work =ESPN.com| publisher =ESPN Internet Ventures| date =March 27, 2014| url =https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/team/schedule/_/id/119/towson-tigers| access-date =April 1, 2014}}</ref> The 25 wins is a program record for their Division I era.<ref name=CITLOSS>{{cite web| title =Towson's Record-Setting Season Comes to a Close | work =TowsonTigers.com| publisher =Towson University| date =March 27, 2014| url =http://www.towsontigers.com/ViewArticle.dbml?SPSID=101525&SPID=12510&DB_LANG=C&ATCLID=209446713&DB_OEM_ID=21300| access-date =April 1, 2014}}</ref> Towson, seeded second in the [[2014 CAA men's basketball tournament|2014 CAA tournament]], was upset in the semifinals by third-seeded [[2013–14 William & Mary Tribe men's basketball team|William & Mary]], ending their chance at an automatic [[NCAA Men's Division I Basketball Championship|NCAA tournament]] bid.<ref name=SCHED/> The Tigers accepted an invitation to play in the [[2014 CollegeInsider.com Postseason Tournament]], however, and won their first two games before falling in the quarterfinals against [[2013–14 Murray State Racers men's basketball team|Murray State]].<ref name=SCHED/> For the year, Benimon averaged 18.7 points, 11.2 rebounds (second best in the nation behind [[2013–14 UC Santa Barbara Gauchos men's basketball team|UC Santa Barbara]]'s [[Alan Williams (basketball)|Alan Williams]]), 3.6 assists, and 1.2 blocks per game.<ref name=SR/> Benimon's 404 total rebounds set a new school single-season record; it also ranks second all-time in CAA men's basketball history.<ref name=CITLOSS/> For the second straight season, Benimon was voted to the CAA's All-Defensive Team as well as being named the CAA Player of the Year.<ref>{{cite web| title =Prewitt, Rusthoven, Thornton Highlight W&M Men's Basketball CAA Award Winners| work =WYdaily.com| publisher =Williamsburg Yorktown Daily| date =March 6, 2014| url =http://wydaily.com/2014/03/06/prewitt-rusthoven-thornton-highlight-wm-mens-basketball-caa-award-winners/| access-date =April 1, 2014| archive-date =April 7, 2014| archive-url =https://web.archive.org/web/20140407065139/http://wydaily.com/2014/03/06/prewitt-rusthoven-thornton-highlight-wm-mens-basketball-caa-award-winners/| url-status =dead}}</ref>

==Professional career==

===2014–15 season===
After going undrafted in the [[2014 NBA draft]], Benimon joined the [[Miami Heat]] for [[Orlando Summer League]]<ref>[http://www.nba.com/heat/heat-announce-summer-league-information-0 HEAT Announce Summer League Information]</ref> and the [[Denver Nuggets]] for the [[NBA Summer League|Las Vegas Summer League]].<ref>[http://www.nba.com/nuggets/2014-summer-league-roster 2014 Summer League Roster] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140711192855/http://www.nba.com/nuggets/2014-summer-league-roster |date=2014-07-11 }}</ref> On September 30, 2014, he signed with the Nuggets,<ref>{{cite web|title=Denver Nuggets Announce 2014-15 Training Camp Roster|url=http://www.nba.com/nuggets/denver-nuggets-announce-2014-15-training-camp-roster|work=NBA.com|date=September 30, 2014|access-date=September 30, 2014}}</ref> but was later waived by the team on October 22 before the start of the [[2014–15 NBA season]].<ref>[http://www.nba.com/nuggets/news/nuggets-waive-benimon-and-williams Nuggets Waive Benimon and Williams]</ref> On November 18, he was acquired by the [[Idaho Stampede]] of the [[NBA Development League]].<ref>{{cite web | title=Stampede Acquires Free Agent Jerrelle Benimon | website=OurSports Central | date=November 18, 2014 | url=https://www.oursportscentral.com/services/releases/stampede-acquires-free-agent-jerrelle-benimon/n-4895936 | access-date=April 19, 2026}}</ref> On February 4, he was named to the Futures All-Star team for the 2015 [[NBA Development League All-Star Game|NBA D-League All-Star Game]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://dleague.nba.com/news/nba-development-league-all-star-game-rosters-2015/|title=Thirteen NBA Veterans Headline Rosters for NBA Development League All-Star Game Presented by Kumho Tire|date=February 15, 2015|work=NBA.com|access-date=July 27, 2015|archive-date=February 5, 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150205023335/http://dleague.nba.com/news/nba-development-league-all-star-game-rosters-2015/|url-status=dead}}</ref>

On March 6, 2015, Benimon signed a 10-day contract with the [[Utah Jazz]].<ref>{{cite web | title=Jazz Sign Jerrelle Benimon to 10-Day Contract | website=NBA.com | date=March 6, 2015 | url=https://www.nba.com/jazz/news/jazz-sign-jerrelle-benimon-10-day-contracts | access-date=April 19, 2026}}</ref> Following the expiration of his contract on March 16, he was not offered a second 10-day contract by the Jazz, parting ways with the team after appearing in just two games and returned to the Stampede that same day. On April 22, he was named to the 2015 All-NBA D-League first team and the All-Rookie first team.<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://dleague.nba.com/news/nba-development-league-announces-2014-15-all-league-teams/ |title=NBA Development League Announces 2014-15 All-League Teams |access-date=2015-04-24 |archive-date=2015-04-26 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150426012519/http://dleague.nba.com/news/nba-development-league-announces-2014-15-all-league-teams/ |url-status=dead }}</ref>

===2015–16 season===
In July 2015, Benimon joined the [[Cleveland Cavaliers]] for the [[2015 NBA Summer League]].<ref>{{cite news|title=Cavs Announce 2015 Samsung NBA Summer League Roster|url=http://www.nba.com/cavaliers/releases/summer-league-roster-2015|access-date=July 7, 2015|work=NBA.com|date=July 7, 2015}}</ref> On September 17, he signed with the [[Foshan Dralions]].<ref>{{cite news|title=Jerelle Benimon joins Foshan|url=http://www.asia-basket.com/China/news/421430/Jerelle-Benimon-joins-Foshan|access-date=September 17, 2015|work=Asia-Basket.com|date=September 17, 2015}}</ref>

===2016–17 season===
Benimon joined the [[Brooklyn Nets]] for the [[2016 NBA Summer League]]. On September 10, he signed with [[Qingdao DoubleStar]] of the [[Chinese Basketball Association]].<ref>{{cite news|title=Jerrelle Benimon signs at Qingdao Eagles|url=http://www.asia-basket.com/China/news/462407/Jerrelle-Benimon-signs-at-Qingdao-Eagles|work=Asia-Basket.com|date=September 10, 2016|access-date=October 2, 2016}}</ref> On March 2, 2017, [[Delaware 87ers]] acquired rights to Benimon.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://delaware.dleague.nba.com/news/sevens-acquire-rights-benimon-thames-draft-pick-trades-stars-bulls/|title=SEVENS ACQUIRE RIGHTS TO BENIMON|work=NBA.com|publisher=Turner Sports Interactive, Inc.|date=March 2, 2017|access-date=March 9, 2017|archive-date=March 12, 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170312043619/http://delaware.dleague.nba.com/news/sevens-acquire-rights-benimon-thames-draft-pick-trades-stars-bulls/|url-status=dead}}</ref>

===2017–18 season===
On October 29, 2017, Benimon signed with German club [[ratiopharm Ulm]].<ref>{{cite news|title=Jerrelle Benimon inks with Ulm|url=https://www.sportando.com/en/germany/bbl/251861/jerrelle-benimon-inks-with-ulm.html|access-date=October 30, 2017|work=Sportando.com|date=October 29, 2017}}</ref>

===2018–19 season===
On August 15, 2018, Benimon signed with the [[New Zealand Breakers]] for the [[2018–19 NBL season]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nbl.com.au/news/article/43338-breakers-complete-roster-with-benimon|title=Breakers Complete Roster With Benimon|work=NBL.com.au|date=August 15, 2018|access-date=August 15, 2018|archive-date=August 18, 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180818093139/http://nbl.com.au/news/article/43338-breakers-complete-roster-with-benimon|url-status=dead}}</ref> He was released by the Breakers on September 3 due to personal issues.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://nbl.com.au/news/article/nz-breakers-release-benimon|title=NZ Breakers Release Jerrelle Benimon|work=NBL.com.au|date=September 3, 2018|access-date=September 3, 2018|archive-date=September 3, 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180903082438/http://nbl.com.au/news/article/nz-breakers-release-benimon|url-status=dead}}</ref>

On January 10, 2019, Benimon signed with [[Bnei Herzliya]] of the [[Israeli Basketball Premier League|Israeli Premier League]] for the rest of the season.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://basket.co.il/news.asp?id=19735|title=בני הרצליה: בנימון במקום ארמסטרונג|work=basket.co.il|date=January 10, 2019|access-date=January 10, 2019|language=he}}</ref>
